outcome: infant neurodevelopment (Bayley mental score, Bayley motor score)
cohort: 160 pregnant women (80 with vitamin D deficiency and 80 matched controls with sufficient vitamin D) who gave birth to 160 healthy full-term infants in China.
finding: Maternal vitamin D deficiency (25(OH)D levels less than 50 nmol/L) was independently associated with a higher tendency for lower infant cognitive and motor development scores at 6 months, and significant intergroup differences in infant anthropometry at birth.
